Dangerous quadrant: ocrdiff 0/15, so no cheap route. ~482 pp = ~48 agents. || 2026-09-13 RE-DIAGNOSIS: the 0/15 precision figure is WRONG and must not be used. ocrdiff DOES find real errors here (it flagged p.454 correctly). Two things hid that: (a) ocrdiff drops any divergence whose (kind,tex,scan) triple recurs >2x as "repeated OCR pattern" - but this book has a SYSTEMATIC transcriber fault, o-for-oe with the slash stripped, and the filter hid 24 of its 28 instances, keeping 4; (b) a random 15-draw from the 250 survivors (101 of them the near-worthless DITTO class) caught none of those 4. TWO ERROR POPULATIONS: mechanical (o/oe, characteer/charakteer, electricitet/elektricitet) - the scan text layer is a RELIABLE witness for these, so they can be adjudicated with NO page images and NO agents; and semantic (paraphrase, dropped sentences) - ocrdiff cannot see these at all (the p.405 loss is absent even pre-filter, a long divergence breaks its anchor). PLAN: cheap mechanical pass first, then collate. || 2026-09-13 REPAIR WAVE 1: pp.1-40 collated at the image, 4 agents x 10 pp., 4 OCRDIFF lines recorded. 8 transcriber's errors corrected + 2 printer's errors restored as printed (pp.17,21,24,26,32,34x2,35,37,39). NO dropped/added/paraphrased words found in pp.1-40; real-error rate there ~0.25/pg, not 1.17 - but all six sampled pages lay in the later book, so this bounds nothing beyond p.40. || THE MECHANICAL PASS IS WITHDRAWN. The plan's premise - that the scan's text layer is a reliable witness for the o/oe class - is FALSE. Unfiltered ocrdiff gives 68 diacritic-only divergences running in BOTH directions (hoiere->hoeiere 11x, hoeiere->hoiere 5x); the Google Fraktur layer mangles the slash itself (Fornvielse for Fornoeielse, Raven for Raeven). Do not restart it. || AND one reader cannot settle the class either: of 16 oe->o claims by collation agents on pp.21-40, a blind two-reader pass (vowel masked in headword and context, same-page calibration, UNREADABLE allowed) confirmed 3, REFUTED 4, found 2 unreadable, and split on 7. The two blind readers agreed with each other on only 42 of 61 sites. Two agents over pp.1-20 raised no such claims at all. Only both-say-PLAIN was applied; the blind pass also found 2 genuine plain glyphs the collation agents missed. Protocol recorded in the book's RESUME-NOTES and transcription.tex header. || 2026-09-13 WAVE 2: pp.41-80 collated, 4 more OCRDIFF lines (8 of 8 waves). 4 transcriber's errors + 2 printer's readings restored (pp.43,45,58x2,67). Again NO dropped/added/paraphrased words. The blind pass cleared ALL 15 OSLASH sites raised by the readers - 17 of 18 glyphs SLASH from both blind readers, file right at every one, nothing changed; blind-reader agreement 17/18 here vs 42/61 in wave 1, the difference being that these were asked as 'what did you see?' rather than as claims to confirm. Keep that framing. NB neither of wave 2's best finds (p.43 Grandser, p.45 Guult) was among the ocrdiff candidates - the text layer had normalised both silently. || CUMULATIVE pp.1-80: 12 transcriber's errors, 4 printer's readings restored, 0 word losses; ~0.2/pg. The 1.17/pg sample drew all six pages from pp.69-454 and found its errors at pp.363/405/454, so the early gatherings look much better than the late ones. NOTHING SO FAR BOUNDS pp.81-482. || 2026-09-13 WAVE 3: pp.81-160 collated, 8 more OCRDIFF lines (16 of 16 waves). Applied 11 o/oe readings restored, 1 PAGE MARKER MOVED (p.107 sat at the wrong 'Egen-' of two on the leaf, ~2.5 printed lines early - pp.106/107 were both mis-cited; invisible to every automatic check since markers were complete and consecutive), 2 emphasis runs split (p.139: 'til' is tight in BOTH phrases, the file had regularised the compositor), 1 header comment corrected (p.105 head is antiqua, not Fraktur). Still NO dropped/added/paraphrased words. || FAT-FACE IS THE SAME PROBLEM AS o/oe. Six halbfette claims on pp.151-158 + a proposal to strip an existing \textbf: the two blind readers split COMPLETELY (one called 7 of 9 passages fat-face, the other called all 9 NONE; the second normalised stem width by x-height and showed the 'heavy' words sit in heavier-inked line bands with unchanged advance, with a real fat-face control at 0.32-0.35 vs 0.21-0.26 at the claimed sites). Nothing applied. Amend the brief: FATFACE is reported, never proposed. || REFUTED: p.148 'Miisforstaaelsen' - both blind readers found ONE dotted i in all three Mis- words; the Fraktur capital M's third stroke is a dotless stem that reads as an i when thin. Expect this wherever M precedes i. || TWO CONFLICTS LEFT OPEN, file unchanged: p.115 'toerre' (blind readers PLAIN vs the file's own documented 600dpi reading that it is slashed) and p.155 'Omboininger' (blind readers SLASH vs the file's documented reading that it is plain). A documented positive reading is not overturned by two blind glyph readings; both need a third with the prior findings in view. || BLIND-PASS PRECISION, measured: reader agreement 8/14, 11/17, 3/17 across the three sets - good enough to REFUTE a claim, only just good enough to sustain one. Hence both-agree-only, and hence the conflicts stand. || CUMULATIVE pp.1-160: 23 transcriber's errors, 4 printer's readings restored, 1 marker moved, 2 emphasis runs, and ZERO word losses in 160 pages - against a 6-page sample that scored 1.17/pg on a paraphrase and a dropped sentence at p.405 plus errors at pp.363/454. Either the damage is concentrated in the late gatherings or the sample was unlucky; pp.161-482 decide it, and the sample says expect the worst around pp.360-460. || 2026-09-13 WAVE 4: pp.161-240 collated, 8 more OCRDIFF lines (24 of 24 waves). Applied 2 printer's readings restored (p.176 Noedvenoighed, p.216 Udviting), 1 transcriber's error (p.232 fremdrage), 10 o/oe restorations, 4 emphasis runs corrected (pp.218/219, 221x2, 223 - the p.223 note asserting 'post rem is letterspaced antiqua' was wrong and is corrected). Still NO dropped/added/paraphrased words. || THE BLIND PASS CORRECTED THE COLLATION READERS TWICE, not merely confirmed/refuted: p.216 was reported 'Udviking' (l wanting) but the sort carries a crossbar and is a t -> 'Udviting'; pp.218/219 was reported as a run breaking mid-word at the line end, but 'Mod-' measures as tight as the 'Modsaetning' below it and only the four nouns are spaced - the proposed fix would have been a NEW error. || OPEN, NOTHING CHANGED: THE STANDING \textbf{} MARKUP IS IN DOUBT. Three agents independently measured ~20 EXISTING fat-face runs on pp.189-216 by stem width normalised to line x-height against same-line plain controls: every one falls in the 0.10-0.27 plain band with word advance matching to the pixel, where a real halbfette control measures 0.32-0.35. Best explanation offered: the heaviness tracks the SORT - the Fraktur 'er' prints heavy everywhere and many \textbf runs here are a single 'er'. This is an edition-wide claim and cuts both ways (the same measure scored a known-fat 'ikke' below a plain 'Saetninger' on p.156). NEEDS ITS OWN PASS with a real halbfette control per leaf; do not let a collation wave drift into it. || Blind-reader agreement this wave: 6/6 on word+spacing questions, 11/14, 10/13, 12/12 on the o/oe sets (first perfect set). Set N gave ZERO changes - all six capital-OE sites on pp.172-173, where the Fraktur capital's flourish sits where a slash would, came back SLASH from both. || ALSO OPEN: p.193 display head is letterspaced in print across both halves and the file marks no Sperrsatz (edition-wide convention question); p.236 stray raised mark after 'et' (one reader only, not blind-verified, not entered). || CUMULATIVE pp.1-240 = HALF THE BOOK: 24 transcriber's errors, 6 printer's readings restored, 21 o/oe restorations, 1 marker moved, 6 emphasis runs, and STILL ZERO word losses in 240 pages against a 6-page sample that scored 1.17/pg. The sample's errors were at pp.363/405/454 - all still ahead. pp.241-482 are now the whole question. || 2026-09-14 COVERAGE IS NOW A RANGE MAP, NOT A RESUME POINT - collation is deliberately out of order. COLLATED pp.1-240. OUTSTANDING pp.241-359 and pp.461-482. NEXT pp.360-460 (the region the 6-page sample implicated: its errors were at pp.363/405/454, and 240 pages have produced zero word-level losses, so that block is the cheapest test of whether the damage is localised). Do NOT call this book repaired until the UNION of collated ranges is exactly 1-482; a page total is not a coverage claim. Check the seams 359|360 and 460|461 for run-over footnotes when the gaps close. || 2026-09-14 WAVE 5, pp.360-459 (OUT OF ORDER, the block the sample implicated): THE HYPOTHESIS HELD. Word-level losses per 100 pp: pp.1-240 ZERO, pp.360-459 FOUR. The 6-page sample was not unlucky - it drew 3 of its 6 pages from this block and found errors on all three. 34 words recovered: p.360 body (6 words, EYE-SKIP on a repeated phrase, left grammatical Danish behind); p.360 footnote (whole opening sentence dropped AND the next clause paraphrased so its sense REVERSED - 'Den store Lighed' had become 'Forskjellen'); p.444 (a clause stood INSIDE a %-comment and was absent from every build - source right, PDF wrong, invisible to every check we have); p.405 afspille/afpille. Plus 8 word corrections (pp.365x2 Elektricitet/Charakteer - the predicted mechanical class - 380, 381, 410, 411, 443x2, 454 full stop -> QUESTION MARK) and 12 emphasis runs incl. 4 SPURIOUS \emph removed from p.446 where both blind readers found no Sperrsatz on the leaf at all. || Blind pass REFUTED 2 claims (p.405 'Skuld', p.413 run extension - file was right) and SPLIT on 2 (p.373 Udtryk/Udtyk, p.372 antiqua extent). || o/oe and fat-face blind passes DEFERRED per the cost note; ~45 o/oe and ~14 fat-face sites are listed by page and word in the book's RESUME-NOTES so a later pass need not re-read the pages. Most fat-face sites DISPUTE an existing \textbf. || COVERAGE: collated pp.1-240 and 360-459. OUTSTANDING pp.241-359 and 460-482 = 142 pages, and the clean early result licenses NOTHING about them. || 2026-09-14 WAVE 6, pp.460-482 (end of book): NO lost text and no word-level error in 23 pages. One emphasis boundary corrected (p.464 run begins at 'stoerre' not 'Trykket'). TWO printer's errors proposed and BOTH REFUTED by the blind pass (p.472 bevtraegt, p.474 goae) - in each case a stroke that did not print, read as a different sort. That is THREE refutations of that shape counting p.405 Skuld/Skyld: ON THIS SCAN AN ABSENT FEATURE IS NEVER SUFFICIENT EVIDENCE FOR A DIFFERENT LETTER. || END OF BOOK VERIFIED: p.482 ends at '(Phil. Propaed. S. 98.)', the file ends there, and PDF 499-502 are blank - no colophon, imprint, errata leaf or advertisements exist in this copy, so nothing printed is missing. || FIRST POSITIVE FAT-FACE RESULT: p.463 gives a genuine WITHIN-LINE control (naestendeels 14px, ganske 13px vs men 10px, aldrig 9px, same line same size) CONFIRMING the file's existing \textbf there; pp.477/479 rubrics show the same within-line contrast at 0.293/0.302 while falling below wave 3's 0.32-0.35 band. The threshold was probably set too high and the right test is WITHIN-LINE contrast, not an absolute ratio - so some of the ~14 disputed \textbf sites may prove correct. Nothing changed. || COVERAGE: collated pp.1-240, 360-482 = 363 of 482. OUTSTANDING pp.241-359 ONLY (119 pp). Lost passages by block: 1-240 ZERO, 360-459 FOUR, 460-482 ZERO - so the damage is NOT the later gatherings in general but pp.360-459 specifically, which leaves pp.241-359 genuinely open: it sits between a clean block and a dirty one and neither result predicts it. || 2026-09-19 WAVE 7 pp.241-359 + REPAIR COMPLETE. ALL 482 PAGES COLLATED, 37 waves, 37 OCRDIFF lines (the count now matches the wave count, which is TRANSCRIPTION-PLAYBOOK section 0's condition for calling a book complete). Wave 7 found ONE lost passage (p.350, six words dropped between two 'de'; the verb after 'Forsoeg' remains split three ways and is left as the file had it) plus 6 other corrections. Wave 7 REFUTED two POSITIVE-SIGNAL claims (p.291 Skittelse, p.292 skjendt) - it is not only absent-ink claims that fail, which is the strongest argument in the programme for the two-reader rule. || WHOLE-PROGRAMME RESULT: 39 words net recovered across 57 change sites. SIX passages of lost/corrupted text, ALL in the second half: p.350 (6 words, eye-skip), p.360 body (6 words, eye-skip), p.360 note (sentence dropped + clause paraphrased so sense REVERSED), p.405 x2 (one from the original sample), p.444 (7 words swallowed by a %-comment - absent from every build though the source was right). Distribution of lost passages: pp.1-240 ZERO, pp.241-359 ONE, pp.360-459 FOUR, pp.460-482 ZERO. || POST-REPAIR RE-MEASUREMENT (5C), seed |post, pp.59/256/285/342/470/481: ZERO confirmed word errors; the one candidate (p.342 full stop vs comma) did NOT survive the blind pass. 0 in 6 pp bounds the residual rate at <=0.50/pg (95%) against 1.17/pg pre-repair. A BOUND, NOT A CERTIFICATE. || STILL OPEN, and the status 'repaired' should be read with these: (1) the o/oe class is DEFERRED - ~130 sites observed, 26 applied, all listed by page and word in RESUME-NOTES so the pass needs no re-reading; every one is a diacritic and none changes a word. (2) FAT-FACE markup in doubt - ~40 existing \textbf runs measure inside the plain band (heaviness tracks the SORT, the Fraktur 'er', not the passage), but p.463 gives a genuine within-line control CONFIRMING the markup there, so wave 3's 0.32-0.35 threshold was probably too high and the right test is within-line contrast. (3) ~12 split or unreadable sites listed in RESUME-NOTES, two of which conflict with this file's own documented readings (p.115 toerre, p.155 Omboininger). || THE RULE THIS BOOK PAID FOR: on this scan AN ABSENT FEATURE IS NEVER SUFFICIENT EVIDENCE FOR A DIFFERENT LETTER - four claimed printer's errors refuted on exactly that (p.405 Skuld, p.472 bevtraegt, p.474 goae, p.342 full stop). Put it in the brief before collating another Google Fraktur scan. | Ø RULE 2026-10-08 (Hans: a plain o in a non-word is a missed ø; CLAUDE.md): 217 sites, 127 word forms, set to ø by oefix.py (German/Latin quotations left); the earlier „as printed“ o/ø convention is superseded; both-word pairs (for/før ...) not touched. | UMLAUT SWEEP 2026-10-09: 1 German umlaut(s) restored (umlaut-sweep-20261009.tsv).
